The son will most likely prevail on answer B. He was an intended donee beneficiary, since the owner promised to pay him and the landscaper meant the payment as a gift. His rights hadn't vested when the parties modified the contract, because he didn't know of it and hadn't relied on it. But the landscaper had already fully performed, and under Restatement (Second) §311 and most courts' approach, a modification that late can't cut off a donee beneficiary's rights, so the owner is still liable.

CONFIDENCE: 62
